doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Performing in Japan
summary: She played hotels and small bars in Japan for six or seven days, booked by Yoshi, to audiences like any other.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: How about touring around the world. I understand you’ve been not only to Europe, but to Africa, Asia and Australia.
I didn’t go to Australia and Africa. But I went to Japan.
Good to know. Tell me about the Japanese audience and how that differs from your experiences in the States and Europe.
They’re just like anybody else. If they move, they hit their derriere. I found that I could move them, too. I was happy about that.
When did you first go to Japan?
About three years ago. I’d gone before as a tourist.
How long did you perform there and where?
Six or seven days, in hotels and little bars no bigger than this. They charge $100 to come in and get a drink.
Who was booking this for you?
